summary: A technically clean, honest Phase 1 whose panel does not fit on its own chassis. Audio is the strong half: one additive four-partial voice, correct pitch E1 (46.9 Hz) to E7 (2636.7 Hz), velocity on pointer (2.04x) and MIDI (3.2x), Space and CC64 sustain, a hard 32-voice ceiling with oldest-first stealing (live oscillators plateau at 128), all-notes-off on blur, node counts back to zero. Pointer, multi-touch, computer keyboard and Web MIDI all reach that one lifecycle. The declared source is what the build does - no audio requests, no decodeAudioData - and 'panel controls are decorative' survives measurement: master level at 0 and Piano Section off leave the strike peak unchanged at 0.06563. The failure is layout: the deck gets 0.476 of instrument height instead of 0.54, so 64 of 161 controls render under the keybed and are clipped away entirely (piano shows 4 of 24, synth 11 of 38); a 5x5 elementFromPoint grid reaches 87 of 161. The visual audit then lists those invisible controls as landmarks exercised and reports the 0.54/0.46 split as achieved, which is where an otherwise scrupulous artifact stops being accurate about itself. The voice also never decays - flat RMS 0.0201 across a one-second hold.

evidence: Pitch is correct across the whole 73-key range in the served build: analyser tap on the destination gives fundamentals of 46.9 Hz at key-28 (E1, 41.2 Hz, one 10.8 Hz bin wide), 257.8 Hz at key-60 (C4, 261.6 Hz) and 2636.7 Hz at key-100 (E7, 2637 Hz), each with partials at exactly 2x/3x/4x.

Level and release behave: pointer strike at the key bottom peaks 0.0656 vs 0.0321 at the key top (2.04x); after key-up RMS falls 0.0133 -> 0.0012 -> 0.00007 -> 0 across ~360 ms, matching a 0.35 s exponential release. 40 simultaneous notes peak at 0.54 with no clipping.

Decay does not behave: holding one key, measured RMS is 0.02148, 0.02012, 0.02010, 0.02012, 0.02011 over five consecutive 200 ms windows - the envelope drops to 55% of peak in 120 ms and then holds flat indefinitely, so a held note sustains like an organ rather than decaying (src/audio/piano-engine.ts noteOn schedules no decay past now+0.12).

Timbre is four fixed-ratio sine partials with identical relative structure at every pitch (no inharmonicity, no register variation, no hammer/attack noise); recognisable as a keyboard tone but thin for a piano.

IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json declares 'Live additive synthesis (sine partials + amplitude envelope)... generated at note-on via Web Audio OscillatorNode; not a recording', sampleSources []. Exercising build/ confirms it: the only network requests for the whole session are index.html plus the two /assets files - no audio fetch at all.

Measured spectrum of a hard C4 strike: fundamental at 257.8 Hz with partials at 527.3/785.2/1043 Hz sitting -9.7/-18.5/-24.4 dB below it - exactly the declared 1, 0.35*vel, 0.12*vel, 0.06 partial set; a soft strike drops the 2nd partial to -16.5 dB relative, matching the velocity-scaled partial gains rather than a sample crossfade.

build/assets/index-eRuA551N.js contains no 'data:audio', no decodeAudioData and no createBufferSource; one createOscillator. The declaration that panel controls are decorative was also verified against the running build (see controlBoundary).

All four input paths reach one lifecycle in the served build. Real mouse press on #key-60 produced RMS 0.0258 with aria-pressed=true and silence (RMS 0) after release. CDP touch: two simultaneous touch points on key-60 and key-67 gave 8 live oscillators (2 voices) and both keys pressed; lifting one left [67] pressed and 4 oscillators live - independent multi-touch works.
page.keyboard.down('h') sounded midi 60 (RMS 0.0228) and set aria-pressed on #key-60; holding it 1.2 s started exactly 4 oscillators (one voice), so key-repeat suppression works.

Web MIDI, driven through the real MidiInput by stubbing navigator.requestMIDIAccess: note-on 0x90 67 120 gave peak 0.0661 and note-on velocity 20 gave 0.0204 (3.2x), CC64 held the note after note-off and released it on CC64=0, data-midi-state read 'connected'; with a NotAllowedError the panel honestly reads MIDI: denied.

The computer-keyboard map is idiosyncratic: it is not chromatic (KeyZ=E2, KeyX=F#2 skips F2) and duplicates pitches (KeyA and Comma both 52, KeyQ and KeyK both 64). With 'k' and 'q' both down, 8 oscillators sound; releasing 'q' clears #key-64's aria-pressed to false while a voice for that pitch is still sounding.
Velocity maps to level on every path: pointer y-position 2.04x (0.0656 vs 0.0321 peak), MIDI velocity 120 vs 20 gives 3.2x (0.0661 vs 0.0204).

Sustain works from both required sources and is truthful: Space held while releasing 'k' kept RMS at 0.0210, and releasing Space dropped it to 0; MIDI CC64=127 held RMS 0.0207 after note-off and CC64=0 silenced it. Space still sustains while a panel button holds focus (the button also toggles, aria-pressed false->true).

Voice stealing is deterministic and bounded: firing 40 MIDI notes, live oscillator count climbs 4, 8, ... 128 and then plateaus at exactly 128 (32 voices x 4 partials), oldest-first per src/audio/piano-engine.ts.

Cleanup is complete: after releasing all 40 notes live oscillators return to 0 and 0 keys remain pressed; a window blur while a note sounds takes RMS 0.0229 -> 0 with 0 pressed keys; over the whole session started == stopped == 224.

Two rough edges: a stolen voice is forceStop()ed with no release ramp (audible click at the polyphony limit), and the visual keybed showed 40 keys pressed while only 32 voices were sounding, so the panel over-reports what is playing.

Visible controls move and report state: focusing #synth-filter-freq and pressing ArrowUp six times (one event per frame) moved aria-valuenow 60 -> 90, exactly 6 x 5%; buttons toggle aria-pressed and their LED class; faders, drawbars, wheel and pitch stick all carry role=slider with live aria-valuenow.

The decorative boundary is honest and verified against the audio, not the source: driving #perf-master-level to aria-valuenow=0 left a subsequent strike at peak 0.06563 (identical to the peak with the knob at default), toggling #piano-section-on off left peak 0.06563, and toggling the decorative #piano-sustped did not sustain a note (0 live voices after note-off). The panel carries a permanent 'Panel controls are decorative (Phase 1)' legend.

Caveat: 64 of 161 controls never render inside their section box, so their inertness cannot be seen and a pointer cannot operate them at all (charged under panelControlCoverage rather than twice). They remain keyboard-operable - focusing #piano-type-grand scrolls the clipped container and moves it from top 530.5 into the section, which is also why a framework click would falsely report success.

The DOM inventory is complete: 161 controls with stable IDs across all six sections - 9 drawbars with LED ladders, organ models/percussion, six piano types plus model/KB Touch/Dyn Comp/Timbre/Unison/Soft Release/String Res, 8 program buttons with dial and page nav, synth osc/filter/env/LFO/arp, six effect units and layer focus, mod wheel and pitch stick, and exactly two data-primary-oled elements (Program and Synth).

But at 1440x900 most of that inventory is not on the panel: measuring each control's box against its section box, 77 of 161 are fully visible, 20 partly, and 64 are entirely clipped - piano 4 visible of 24 (every type selector, model knob, KB Touch, Timbre, Unison, Soft Release, String Res clipped), synth 11 of 38 (all filter, envelope, LFO and arp controls clipped), organ 19 of 33, program 13 of 23, effects 22 of 35, performance 8 of 8.

The 5x5 elementFromPoint grid at 1440x900 unscrolled resolves 87 of 161 controls to themselves or a descendant; the other 74 resolve to a piano key, the bottom rail or the app shell, i.e. they are laid out under the keybed and clipped by .section-controls { overflow: hidden }.

Placement bug against the variant photo: the spec puts the rotary speaker block on the exposed red chassis of the performance band, but organ-rotary-speed / organ-rotary-stop are rendered inside the Organ plate (and are themselves clipped).

piano.basic-note-lifecycle, basic-inputs and basic-sustain-polyphony are all demonstrable in the served build, not just in tests: note on/off, overlapping and repeated notes, 0.35 s release to silence, 32-voice ceiling with oldest-first stealing, all-notes-off on blur, and node counts returning to baseline (live oscillators 0, started == stopped == 224).

piano.basic-status-cleanup is mostly truthful: data-audio-status reads 'loading' before the first gesture, 'ready' once the context resumes, and 'error' when AudioContext construction is made to throw (status bar text 'Audio: error'); MIDI reports pending/connected/denied/disconnected correctly.

Gap: there is no labeled playable fallback. With audio broken the keybed does not even show pressed state (aria-pressed stays false on a real mouse press) because noteOn returns an empty id; the 'fallback' status in src/audio/piano-engine.ts is only set if createContext throws once then succeeds, which cannot happen in practice.

The feature matrix maps all 11 Phase 1 IDs to non-empty test files (12 files, 32 tests, all passing on a clean install), but the audio assertions are state-only against a mock context - tests/piano-sustain-polyphony.test.ts 'velocity' case asserts getActiveVoiceCount() === 2 and never that a louder velocity yields a larger signal, which the task's audio test rules explicitly disallow.

The audio declarations hold exactly: live synthesis with no bundled samples (no audio requests, no decodeAudioData in the bundle), 'panel controls are decorative and do not alter the audio graph' (master level at 0 and Piano Section off both leave the strike peak at 0.06563), and 'sustain responds to Space, MIDI CC64 and engine API only - not decorative panel toggles' (the piano-sustped toggle left 0 live voices after note-off, while Space and CC64 both held).

But evidence/stage1-visual-audit.md claims landmarks that the sealed build does not show: 'Piano: type selectors, model knob, layer levels, timbre/detail switches' and 'Synth: ... osc/filter/env/LFO/arp groups' are listed as exercised, while at the captured 1440x900 viewport 19 of 24 piano and 21 of 38 synth controls are clipped entirely out of view. The clipping appears in none of the seven Known deviations.

The same audit asserts geometry the build does not reach: 'Deck / keybed 0.54 / 0.46' - measured deck including the top rail is 0.4759 of instrument height (keybed 0.4738), 0.064 outside the 0.54 +/- 0.025 band, because a 20 px status bar plus fixed 46%/46% flex bases consume the chassis. It also claims the narrow layout uses 'width: 180vw so controls remain inspectable', but the rendered 390x844 instrument measures 386.1 px wide because flex-shrink overrides that rule.

IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md ticks the hard gate 'The complete visible control surface is present' and 'Every visible panel control moves or presses accessibly', which is not true of the 64 controls a pointer cannot reach.

issues.title: 64 of 161 panel controls are clipped entirely out of view at 1440x900
issues.detail: Each .section-controls flow-lays its controls and clips the overflow (overflow: hidden), and the deck is too short to hold them. Measuring every control box against its section box in the served build: 77 fully visible, 20 partly, 64 fully clipped - piano 4 of 24 visible (all six type selectors, model knob, KB Touch, Dyn Comp, Timbre, Unison, Soft Release, String Res invisible), synth 11 of 38 (all filter, envelope, LFO and arp knobs invisible), organ 19 of 33, program 13 of 23, effects 22 of 35. A 5x5 elementFromPoint grid at 1440x900 unscrolled reaches 87 of 161; the remaining 74 hit-test to a piano key, the bottom rail or the app shell. They are still tab-focusable, and focusing one scrolls the hidden container (focusing #piano-type-grand moves it from top 530.5 into the section), so a framework click reports success for controls a person cannot see or reach.

issues.title: Deck vertical allocation is 0.476, not the declared 0.54
issues.detail: Measured in the served build at 1440x900: instrument 1353.59 x 437.33 (aspect 3.0951, width fraction 0.94 - both correct), top rail 6.95, deck 201.17, keybed 200.25, bottom rail 6.95, status bar 20. Deck including the top rail is 0.4759 of instrument height against a 0.54 +/- 0.025 band (2.6x tolerance out); keybed including its rail is 0.4738, inside band. The instrument is a column flex box whose children sum past its aspect-ratio height, so both 54%/46% flex bases are shrunk to ~46% each and the extra 20 px status bar takes the rest. This squeeze is the direct cause of the clipped controls, and evidence/stage1-visual-audit.md still reports the split as 0.54/0.46.

issues.title: Visual audit claims landmarks and a narrow layout the sealed build does not show
issues.detail: evidence/stage1-visual-audit.md lists under 'Landmarks exercised' the piano type selectors, model knob and timbre/detail switches and the synth osc/filter/env/LFO/arp groups; none of those are visible at the captured 1440x900 viewport. Its 'Known deviations' section (seven entries) never mentions that ~40% of the control surface is clipped. It also states the narrow layout uses 'width: 180vw so controls remain inspectable', but the rendered 390x844 instrument measures 386.13 px wide because .app-shell's flex-shrink overrides the rule, leaving roughly five controls visible per section. IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md likewise ticks the hard gates 'The complete visible control surface is present' and 'Every visible panel control moves or presses accessibly'.

issues.title: Held notes never decay
issues.detail: The amplitude envelope ramps to peak in 8 ms, down to 55% of peak by 120 ms, and then holds. Five consecutive 200 ms RMS windows on one held key read 0.02148, 0.02012, 0.02010, 0.02012, 0.02011 - a flat organ-like sustain rather than a piano decay. Release itself is fine (0.35 s exponential to silence).

issues.title: Stolen voices are hard-stopped and the keybed keeps showing them as held
issues.detail: At the 32-voice ceiling PianoEngine.forceStop() calls osc.stop() with no release ramp, so stealing clicks. Firing 40 MIDI notes left 40 keys with is-pressed while only 32 voices (128 oscillators) were sounding, so the panel over-reports what is playing. getActiveNotes() also always reports velocity 0.

issues.title: Audio behaviour is asserted only through a mock context
issues.detail: All 12 test files run in jsdom against src/test/mock-audio.ts. tests/piano-sustain-polyphony.test.ts's velocity case asserts getActiveVoiceCount() === 2 after a 0.1 and a 1.0 velocity note and never that the louder one produces a larger signal; nothing asserts sustain changes duration or that output differs from silence at signal level. The task's audio test rules require signal-direction assertions. The behaviour is genuinely correct in the running build - the tests just do not prove it.

issues.title: Computer-keyboard map is non-chromatic and duplicates pitches
issues.detail: src/input/keyboard.ts maps KeyZ=40, KeyX=42 (skipping F2) and gives two codes the same note in several places (KeyA and Comma both 52, KeyQ and KeyK both 64). Holding 'k' and 'q' together sounds 8 oscillators; releasing 'q' clears #key-64's aria-pressed to false while the other voice is still sounding, because the note map is keyed by midi rather than by code.

issues.title: No labeled playable fallback, and the 'fallback' status is unreachable
issues.detail: With AudioContext construction forced to throw, data-audio-status honestly becomes 'error' and the status bar reads 'Audio: error' - but a real mouse press on a key then leaves aria-pressed false, so the instrument gives no response at all. The 'fallback' state in PianoEngine.init() is only set when createContext throws once and then succeeds on the retry, which cannot occur in practice.

issues.title: Rotary speaker block placed in the Organ plate rather than the performance band
issues.detail: specs/nord-stage-4.visual.json requires 'rotary speaker controls' among the performance-band landmarks on the exposed red chassis (with a photo citation at x 2200-2500 of 11600). The build renders organ-rotary-speed and organ-rotary-stop inside the Organ inset plate, where both are also among the clipped controls.
